short: The guns fell silent at eleven in the morning after four years and three months.
full:
By the autumn of 1918 the German army was retreating everywhere under the Allied Hundred Days offensive, Bulgaria, the Ottoman Empire and Austria-Hungary had left the war, the naval mutiny at Kiel had spread inland, and the Kaiser had abdicated and fled to the Netherlands. A German delegation led by Matthias Erzberger met Marshal Foch in his railway carriage in the forest of Compiegne. The terms were dictated rather than negotiated: withdrawal from all occupied territory, surrender of the fleet and enormous quantities of materiel, and Allied occupation of the Rhineland.

The armistice was signed at about 5.15am on 11 November 1918 and took effect at eleven. Firing continued in places until the last minute; the American Henry Gunther was killed at 10.59. It was a ceasefire and not a peace, and because no Allied soldier stood on German soil it left room for the claim that the army had been stabbed in the back rather than beaten. Hitler had the same carriage brought out for the French surrender in June 1940.
